provenance.paper_title: Do Proactive Agents Really Need an LLM to Decide When to Wake and What to Anchor?

representation_paths.memory_component: causal heterogeneous temporal graph of session events and the files, applications, URLs, queries, and type entities they touch

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3 Problem Formulation and Sec. 4 Method
evidence.paraphrase: At decision time t, observed activity history through t is represented as a heterogeneous temporal graph. Event nodes are linked to named files, applications, URLs, queries, and type nodes, while directional temporal edges connect consecutive events; these named entities remain recoverable and are routed as structured evidence to the downstream agent.

evidence.section: Full paper: Appendix B.1, What the Graph Network Actually Sees
evidence.paraphrase: Inference removes backward temporal edges so each trigger and routing decision depends only on the current event and prior events in its session, making the accumulated session graph a causal operative state rather than future-aware evaluation context.

Structured activity events are deterministically converted into event, entity, type, and temporal-edge updates under the same fixed graph-construction rules at training and inference. Each later event therefore extends the causal session graph that the TGL trigger and routing heads read on subsequent decisions.

adjudication_notes: The manuscript bibliography key proactivewake2026 is only a citation-key shorthand; the paper does not name the architecture ProactiveWake. The record therefore uses the paper's own TGL trigger-and-routing terminology.

T2 is assigned because the operative causal session graph is extended as new deployment events arrive and later trigger/routing decisions consume that accumulated state. The TGL weights, graph-construction rule, trigger threshold, and routing cap remain fixed, so no T3 policy evolution occurs.
